body.statement:
The equal-alphabet subfamily of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), consisting of models in which every observed coordinate has alphabet cardinality \(q\), and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) are incomparable in the ambient mixed-type latent-structure universe.  Within this equal-alphabet subfamily, every selected observed variable has support cardinality \(q\), so Chen et al.'s discrete sufficient-measurement requirement
\[
 \lvert\operatorname{supp}(X_j)\rvert>
 \lvert\operatorname{supp}(H_k)\rvert
\]
cannot hold when the relevant latent coordinate has support cardinality \(q\); the dense ternary witness is therefore outside their two-sufficient-measurement class.  Conversely, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) permits continuous measurements and graphs without two disjoint triangular views, so it is not contained in the equal-alphabet certified subfamily.  Completeness in Chen et al. supplies a discretization with full-rank tables, whereas this project derives full rank from the finite local certificate without assuming completeness or larger-support measurements.
body.justification: The class relation prevents the new certificate from being presented as a disguised instance of completeness or two sufficient measurements.
body.gap: Chen et al. (2025, Proposition 4.2, Definition D.3, and Theorem 4.19) cover mixed-type measurements through completeness and two sufficient measurements, not equal-state double-triangular tables.
body.consumer: It tells practitioners whether a mixed-type tensor-rank guarantee or the local categorical certificate applies to a given item bank.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) denote, only within this proof, the subfamily of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) for which every observed alphabet has cardinality \(q\).  Positive latent support gives, for every \(k\) and \(r\in\mathcal Q\),
\[
 P(H_k=r)=\sum_{h_{-k}\in\mathcal Q^{K-1}}\pi_{(r,h_{-k})}>0.
\]
Consequently \(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(H_k)\rvert=q\).

We next verify the asserted support statement for a selected observed coordinate.  Fix \(j=s(a,k)\).  By the definition of the certificate, all factors \(c_{a,k,u}\) are nonnegative and all their exponents are positive.  Since a member of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) satisfies \(\Delta_{mathrm{DT}}\ne0\), every such factor is nonzero.  In the equal-alphabet case, Definition~\textnormal{def:local-minors} and Theorem~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} give
\[
 c_{a,k,u}=\det(B_{a,k,u})^2>0.
\]
Thus \(B_{a,k,u}\) is invertible.  For any \(x\in\mathcal Q\), its row indexed by \(x\) cannot be zero, so there is an \(r\in\mathcal Q\) with
\[
 L_{a,k,u}(x,r)>0.
\]
The event \(H_{\rho_a(1:k-1)}=u, H_{\rho_a(k)}=r\) has positive probability by positive latent support.  The definition of \(L_{a,k,u}\) therefore yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(X_j=x)
 &\ge
 P\!\left(H_{\rho_a(1:k-1)}=u,
           H_{\rho_a(k)}=r\right)
 L_{a,k,u}(x,r)\\
 &>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Because the alphabet itself has exactly \(q\) states, this proves \(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(X_j)\rvert=q\) for every selected row.  More generally every observed variable in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) is discrete and has support cardinality at most \(q\).

Lemma~\textnormal{lem:chen-mixed-sufficient-measurement} records that a discrete sufficient measurement in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) must have support strictly larger than that of its latent parent and that every latent-parent set must have two such measurements.  In \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), the latent-parent support has cardinality \(q\), whereas every observed support has cardinality at most \(q\).  Hence no observed variable in this subfamily can satisfy that strict support inequality, and the two-sufficient-measurement requirement fails.

The equal-alphabet certified subfamily is nonempty.  Proposition~\textnormal{prop:ternary-witness}, using Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense}, produces a faithful rational perturbation on the displayed graph \(\Gamma^{\star}\) with ternary observed alphabets and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\).  It belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), but the preceding support argument excludes it from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\).  Thus \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\not\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\).

For the reverse noncontainment, Lemma~\textnormal{lem:chen-mixed-sufficient-measurement} states that the mixed class permits continuous sufficient measurements and multifactor measurement graphs without the two-disjoint-triangular-view restriction.  Any admissible member having a continuous observed coordinate is outside \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), because every observed coordinate in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) has a finite \(q\)-point alphabet.  Hence \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\not\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), proving incomparability.

Finally, the same cited lemma states that Chen et al.'s completeness condition supplies a discretization with a full-rank conditional table.  In contrast, in the present subfamily full rank follows algebraically from \(\Delta_{mathrm{DT}}\ne0\): Theorem~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} gives full column rank of both triangular-view matrices, and Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} makes this equivalent to the nonvanishing local determinants in the equal-alphabet case.  Thus the two rank mechanisms asserted in the statement are distinct, and all parts of the narrowed claim follow.
